question: The device used for measuring potential difference across the ends of a conductor is:
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Voltmeter**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **voltmeter** is an instrument used to measure the **electric potential difference** between two points in an electric circuit.
 
• It is connected in **parallel** across the component or section of the circuit where the potential difference is to be measured.
 
• Voltmeter has a very high internal **resistance** to ensure that it does not draw significant current from the circuit, which could alter the potential difference being measured.
 
• It is calibrated to show readings in **volts (V)**, the SI unit of potential difference.
 
• Modern voltmeters can be either **analog** or **digital**, with digital voltmeters providing more precise readings.
 
• They are widely used in **electrical engineering**, **electronics**, and many industrial applications for troubleshooting and testing circuits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ammeter**__

 __
 
• An **ammeter** is used to measure **electric current** in a circuit and is connected in **series** to the circuit.
 
• It has very low internal **resistance** to ensure the current flow is not significantly altered.
 
 
 
• **Battery**__
 __
 
• A **battery** is a device that stores **chemical energy** and converts it into **electrical energy** to provide power to circuits.
 
• It is not used for measuring electrical quantities but rather for **powering electrical devices.**
 
 
 
• **Galvanometer**__
 
 
• A **galvanometer** is used to detect and measure **small electric currents**.
 
• It is a very sensitive instrument and is often used in **laboratory settings**.
 
• Galvanometers can be adapted into ammeters or voltmeters by adding appropriate shunts or series resistances.
